title: Orange, Asparagus, and Avocado Salad
description: This Spanish salad is bright and beautiful. The combination of oranges and tomatoes offers a nice, tangy complement to the rich avocado and asparagus flavors.
ingredients: 4 oz romaine lettuce (cut into bite-size pieces)
1 large orange (peeled and cut into segments)
1 large beefsteak tomatoes (cut into 12 equal pieces)
steps: Place asparagus in a pot of boiling water over high heat. Reduce heat to low and simmer until asparagus is tender, about 10 minutes. Drain asparagus and submerge immediately in a bowl of ice water.
Divide lettuce evenly among six salad bowls or plates.
Combine orange, tomato, and avocado in a medium bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper until combined.
Drain asparagus and add to orange mixture. Pour dressing over orange mixture and stir gently to combine. Spoon mixture on top of romaine lettuce on plates and serve.

title: Lemon Herbed Chicken
description:
Delight your palate with our Lemon Herbed Chicken, a dish that perfectly balances zest and herbs for a refreshing taste. This summer-ready recipe begins with a homemade marinade of lemon zest, fresh lemon juice, and a blend of garlic and thyme. The chicken is then pan-seared to golden perfection, accompanied by aromatic lemon slices.

Each serving is drizzled with the warm, flavorful sauce and garnished with a sprinkle of fresh herbs. With a prep time of 30 minutes and a cook time of 25 minutes, this dish serves four, making it a perfect choice for a nutritious family meal. Each serving contains 220 calories and is rich in protein, ensuring a satisfying and healthy meal.
ingredients: 2 whole Juice of Lemon (juiced and zested)
steps: Prep the Marinade: In a small pot, warm the lemon zest, lemon juice, 2 tablespoons of olive oil, minced garlic, chopped thyme, kosher salt, and black pepper to create the sauce.

Heat the remaining tablespoon of oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and lemon slices to the skillet. Cook the chicken until it’s golden brown and reaches an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C), about 5 minutes a side.
Serve the chicken and lemon slices with the warm sauce and garnish with additional fresh herbs.

title: Arugula and Pear Salad with Walnuts
description: Savor the exquisite blend of flavors in our Arugula and Pear Salad with Walnuts. Peppery arugula is perfectly complemented by the sweetness of ripe pears and the crunch of walnuts, creating a delightful and diabetes-friendly side salad.
steps: In a large bowl, combine the arugula, pears, walnuts, and blue cheese.
In a small bowl, whisk together the balsamic vinegar, olive oil, Dijon mustard, honey, salt, and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the salad and gently toss to ensure even coating.

title: Broiled Cod
description: The American Diabetes Association and the American Heart Association recommend eating at least 2 servings of fish per week. This broiled cod is a tasty option. If you’re not a fan of cod, feel free to substitute any fish here. Click here for more heart-healthy recipes
steps: Preheat broiler. Spray a baking sheet or broiler pan with cooking spray.
In a small bowl mix together mayonnaise, lemon juice, paprika, parsley and ground black pepper.
Place cod filets on broiler pan and spread mayonnaise mixture evenly among the cod filets. Sprinkle Parmesan cheese on top of filets.
Broil filets for 8-10 minutes.

title: Peach and Ginger Granita
description: This diabetes-friendly dessert features refreshing peach and ginger granita with bright lemon and maple flavor, making it a light, satisfying frozen treat.
ingredients: 4 med peaches (ripe, peeled, pitted, and quartered)
steps: In a blender, combine the peaches, ginger, maple syrup, and fresh lemon juice.
Blend the mixture until it becomes a smooth purée.
Pour the peach and ginger purée in an even layer into a shallow freezer-safe pan.
Place the dish in the freezer and let it set for about 1 hour.
After 1 hour, use a fork to scrape the frozen edges into the center. Repeat this process every 30 minutes for the next 3–4 hours or until the entire mixture is granular and frozen.
Once the granita has reached the desired texture, scoop and serve in small bowls.
